note: Known, deliberately tolerated secret-scanner findings. scripts/secret-scan.sh scans the pushed range and the working tree (or, with --all, the whole history), and FAILS on any finding not listed here. A hit is covered when some entry's "rule" equals the hit's rule AND that entry's "path" equals the hit's repo-relative path — so a new occurrence of the same rule in a different file still fails. An entry that matches nothing is reported as stale, so suppression that has outlived its subject is visible rather than silent. Never disposition a finding by disabling a rule or excluding a path class: docs are where real credentials get pasted. Report findings by rule, path, line and commit only — never by value.

entry_shape.rule: the scanner's rule id (RuleID in gitleaks JSON)
entry_shape.path: repo-relative path of the file the finding is in
entry_shape.reason: why this occurrence is not a credential (required)
entry_shape.commit: the commit the occurrence was dispositioned at (informational)
entry_shape.recorded: when and how it was established (informational)
